Description
The Policy & Access Control Engineering (PACE) team, under Operations Infrastructure Services (OIS) organization is looking for an experienced System Development Engineer to join team in Austin. The PACE team provides network security solutions to Amazon fulfillment centers (FCs) using Access Control Lists (ACLs) deployed on on premise firewall as well as cloud firewall devices. ACLs act as a gatekeeper, allowing or blocking network traffic flow in and out of FCs based on predefined rules. Changes in the underlying infrastructure necessitate updates in deployed ACLs to ensure seamless operation of FC solutions. To maintain the right security posture while enabling FC solutions to get network connectivity within defined Service Level Agreements (SLA), the PACE team focuses on two aspects: 1) ACL Freshness: the frequency with which ACLs are deployed to network devices, 2) ACL effectiveness: determines if the ACLs defined by the FC solutions using OIS tools are used effectively and are not adding unnecessary complexity to the OIS network.

Proactively identify and address technical debt, architectural limitations, and performance bottlenecks, proposing and implementing refactoring and optimization strategies to improve the systems' efficiency and maintainability.
Ensure robust monitoring, alerting, and troubleshooting mechanisms are in place for the ACL management systems.
Give careful consideration of availability, operations, maintenance, and cost.

Program Overview
The BD Engineering Development Program (EDP) is designed to give new engineering graduates an opportunity to spend the first three years of their career rotating through three different BD businesses throughout the US. EDPs work side by side with R&D engineers on cross-functional teams to design, develop, and manufacture a wide range of medical devices, growing their BD network with each successive rotation. Following the completion of the program, EDP’s progress into a full-time position in one of the BD R&D groups based on their interests and business needs.
Potential rotation locations include:
Vernon Hills, IL; Irvine, CA; Brea, CA; Salt Lake City, UT; Franklin Lakes, NJ; Warwick, RI; Tempe, AZ; Research Triangle Park, NC; Durham, NC; San Diego, CA; Covington, GA; Louisville, CO
Job Description
An EDP is a results-driven individual who continuously seeks to improve, presents a positive and professional demeanor, and is willing to learn about BD medical device instrumentation and applications.
A successful candidate will work under the supervision of an R&D manager and team to develop and maintain medical technology and devices. They work to design, develop, and test medical devices while following medical device regulations and quality processes. An EDP will also collaborate with stakeholders, analysts, scientists, and quality, regulatory, and marketing groups to understand patient and healthcare provider needs and realize them in new technology. Participation in design reviews, device testing, and providing regular status updates is expected.

New engineering graduates with a BS or MS in Mechanical, Biomedical (Bioengineering), Materials, Electrical, Chemical, or related discipline

Critical decision maker using basic engineering principles

Experience writing technical protocols and reports

Demonstrated comprehension of basic comparative statistics
